about: Battle of Readers (Henry, Nov 19; replaces Reading Island): the shared Battle engine with a story per round (games/shared/stories.json). hidden = the hidden bonuses (2 per round). Only slides and bonuses live here.

intro.title: Battle of Readers
text: Each round: read a short story together.
Then answer 5 questions. Your team writes each answer on ONE board.

intro.title: Read carefully!
text: When the questions start, the story goes away.
Your teacher can show it again with 📖 Story.

intro.title: 3 kinds of questions
text: Write T or F, a short answer, or the correct word.

intro.title: Check together
text: After 5 questions, we check every answer together.

intro.title: Count your points
text: 1 point for each right answer, plus your bonuses.
Tell your teacher your team’s total.

hidden.name: Golden Question
hidden.text: Question {n} was secretly worth double! Right? +1 more.

hidden.name: Comeback
hidden.text: The team in last place gets +2!

hidden.name: Neatest Board
hidden.text: Your teacher picks the neatest board: +2!

hidden.name: Spelling Star
hidden.text: Every word on your board spelled right? +2!

hidden.name: Full Sentence
hidden.text: One answer written as a full sentence? +1!

hidden.name: Story Detective
hidden.text: Tell the class one more detail from the story: +1!

hidden.name: Remember the Title
hidden.text: Write the story’s title from memory: +1!

hidden.name: Lucky Letter
hidden.text: +1 for each right answer that starts with the letter {letter}!

M.1.q: Why did the writer's family stop thinking Mr. Chai was unfriendly? Use 'because' and give TWO details from the story.
M.1.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.1.answer: Because he helped her mom push the car in the rain and he made hot tea for them, so they saw he is kind and shy.
M.1.why: Two details: he helped push the car, he made hot tea. A 'because' sentence.

read.title: The Quiet Neighbor
sentences: Mr. Chai lives next door to us.
He never says hello, and he always looks angry.
Last week my mom's car broke down in the rain.
Mr. Chai came out with an umbrella and helped her push the car.
Then he made hot tea for all of us.
Now we know he is not unfriendly. He is just shy.

M.1.q: How do you think Anna felt at the end? Give TWO reasons from the story.
M.1.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.1.answer: She felt happy and proud because she did the right thing, and the man was very thankful, even though she didn't get a new phone.
M.1.why: Reasons: she returned the wallet, the man thanked her. Her smile shows she was happy.

read.title: The Lost Wallet
sentences: Anna found a wallet on the bus.
There was a lot of money inside, and she really wanted a new phone.
But she also saw a photo of a little girl and a name card.
Anna called the number on the card.
An hour later, a tired man thanked her again and again.
Anna went home with a big smile and no new phone.

M.1.q: Why did Mia set TWO alarms? Answer in a full sentence and explain the lesson she learned.
M.1.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.1.answer: Because she was nearly late when her alarm didn't ring, she learned she needs a backup so she won't be late again.
M.1.why: A cause and a lesson: one alarm failed, so she wants a backup.

read.title: The Broken Alarm
sentences: Mia's alarm clock did not ring on Monday.
She woke up at 8:00 and her class started at 8:15.
She ran to the bus stop without breakfast.
The bus was just leaving, so she had to run after it.
She arrived at school out of breath, but she was on time.
That night she set TWO alarms.

M.1.q: Write a NEW title for the story and explain why it is a good title.
M.1.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.1.answer: Example: 'A Kind Surprise' because Pim cared about the sick woman and her gift made the woman smile.
M.1.why: Accept any logical title with a reason that matches the story (kindness, caring, a surprise).

read.title: Night Market
sentences: Every Friday, Pim and her dad go to the night market.
They always buy mango sticky rice from the same old woman.
One Friday, the woman was not there.
A boy was selling the rice instead. He said, 'My grandmother is sick today.'
The next Friday, Pim brought a card and a flower for her.
The old woman smiled for the first time in weeks.

M.1.q: How did Ben change from the beginning to the end? Describe BOTH sides with details.
M.1.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.1.answer: At first Ben was alone and shy, but Kate was kind to him, so he made friends and now he helps new students.
M.1.why: Before: alone, ate quickly. After: four friends, helps new students.

read.title: The New Student
sentences: Ben was new at school and did not know anyone.
At lunch he sat alone and ate quickly.
A girl named Kate saw him and sat down next to him.
She asked him about his old school and his favorite game.
By the end of the week, Ben had four new friends.
Now he always looks for new students at lunch.

M.1.q: What would you do in Tom's situation? Give one choice and one reason, and say if it was the same as Tom's.
M.1.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.1.answer: Example: I would also go into the cafe because it was safe and warm; that is what Tom did, too.
M.1.why: Accept any sensible choice with a reason. The comparison with Tom must be correct.

read.title: The Last Bus
sentences: It was 10 p.m. and the last bus had left.
Tom's phone had no battery and the street was dark.
He started to walk home, which took an hour.
On the way, he saw a small cafe that was still open.
The owner let him charge his phone and gave him a free hot chocolate.
Tom called his mom and she came to pick him up.

M.2.q: What is the writer's main message in this story? Support your answer with TWO pieces of evidence.
M.2.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.2.answer: Doing research before acting leads to better results. Evidence: Dara read about hydroponics and added plant food, and her plant grew twice as tall as the others.
M.2.why: Main idea: research first. Evidence: read about hydroponics, plant food each week, plant twice as tall.

read.title: The Experiment
sentences: Dara's science teacher gave the class a challenge: keep a plant alive for a month without using soil.
Most students put their seeds in water and hoped for the best.
Dara, however, read about hydroponics and added tiny amounts of plant food to the water every week.
After three weeks, her plant was twice as tall as everyone else's.
Her teacher asked how she knew what to do.
'I didn't know,' said Dara. 'I just decided to find out first.'

M.2.q: How and why did Nok's attitude change? Explain in 2-3 sentences using details.
M.2.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.2.answer: At first she thought the rule was boring and unfair, but after hearing her grandfather's story she enjoyed talking with him, so she stopped complaining and wanted more stories.
M.2.why: Before: boring/unfair. Trigger: grandfather's story. After: asked for another story, no complaints.

read.title: The Phone-Free Dinner
sentences: In Nok's house, nobody could use a phone at dinner.
Nok thought this rule was boring and unfair.
One evening her grandfather started telling a story about his first job on a fishing boat.
Nok had never heard it before, and she forgot to check her messages for an hour.
Afterwards she asked him to tell another story the next day.
The rule was still the same, but she did not complain again.

M.2.q: What do you think Leo's mother will decide? Make a PREDICTION and support it with two clues from the story.
M.2.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.2.answer: She will probably let the dog stay. Clues: she put a bowl of water down, and she only sighed instead of getting angry.
M.2.why: Prediction with clues: water bowl, sigh/no anger, they slept together.

read.title: The Stray Dog
sentences: A thin brown dog started to follow Leo home from school every day.
Leo's mother said, 'We can't keep a dog. Dogs are expensive.'
So Leo began feeding the dog a little from his lunch and made a bed from old boxes outside the building.
When it rained heavily one night, he quietly let the dog sleep in the hallway.
In the morning his mother found them both asleep.
She sighed, shook her head, and put a bowl of water on the floor.

M.2.q: Why was Sam's unplanned answer successful? Explain what the manager valued.
M.2.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.2.answer: The manager valued honesty and real passion; Sam was truthful and showed he loves the shop, which is better than a rehearsed answer.
M.2.why: Key idea: honesty and genuine interest beat practiced answers.

read.title: The Interview
sentences: Sam was nervous before his first job interview at a bookstore.
He had practiced answers all night, but when the manager asked, 'Why do you want to work here?', his mind went blank.
After a long silence, he said, 'Honestly, I don't know what to say. I just love this place.'
The manager laughed kindly and said, 'That is the best answer today.'
Sam started work the following Monday.

M.2.q: Explain how Ms. Ploy changed the library. Give THREE details showing the effect on the students.
M.2.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.2.answer: She started a Book Swap table, so students shared books, the table emptied daily, and they wrote notes to each other; the library became livelier.
M.2.why: Details: Book Swap, empty table by lunch, notes in books, noisy but welcome.

read.title: The Quiet Library
sentences: The school library was always quiet, and most students used it only to study.
Then a new librarian, Ms. Ploy, put a 'Book Swap' table by the door.
Students could leave a book they had finished and take another one for free.
Within a month, the table was empty by lunchtime every day.
Students began leaving little notes inside the books: 'Loved chapter 3!' or 'The ending will shock you.'
The library was no longer silent, but nobody minded.

M.2.q: Was anyone to blame? Give an opinion with reasons, and say what each person could have done better.
M.2.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.2.answer: The caretaker was partly to blame because he didn't tell anyone; the coach could have asked staff first before worrying everyone. Nobody meant harm.
M.2.why: Accept reasoned opinions: the caretaker should have told someone; others should have asked before assuming.

read.title: The Missing Trophy
sentences: On Monday morning, the soccer trophy was missing from the school cabinet.
The coach looked worried, and everyone wondered who had taken it.
The caretaker explained that he had borrowed it to polish it for Friday's ceremony.
'I should have told someone,' he said.
Everyone laughed with relief.
On Friday, the trophy shone brighter than ever.

M.3.q: What is the author's attitude toward recommendation apps? Support your answer with TWO quotations or details, and explain what they show.
M.3.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.3.answer: The author is critical: the app shows 'whatever kept her watching', not what she liked, and choosing for herself felt strange, which shows the app had been choosing for her.
M.3.why: Attitude: critical/cautious. Evidence: 'whatever kept her watching'; unfollowing and 'felt strange to choose'.

read.title: The Algorithm
sentences: Every evening, Mia's phone suggested videos she would 'probably enjoy', and every evening she watched far more than she had planned.
One night she noticed that all the suggestions were about the same topic, even though she used to love many things.
She realized the app was not showing her what she liked; it was showing her whatever kept her watching.
The next day she unfollowed fifty channels and searched for something completely new.
It felt strange to choose for herself again.

M.3.q: What does the writer mean by 'the strongest bridge'? Explain the literal and the figurative meaning.
M.3.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.3.answer: Literally it is not very strong because it moves in the wind, but figuratively it is strong because it represents the village's unity.
M.3.why: Literal: a simple, slightly moving wooden bridge. Figurative: strength from cooperation.

read.title: The Bridge
sentences: The villagers had wanted a bridge for fifty years, but every plan had failed because nobody could agree on where to build it.
Then a flood destroyed the old path, and, for the first time, the whole village worked together.
They built a simple wooden bridge in three weeks.
It was not perfect; it moved slightly when the wind blew.
Yet the elders said it was the strongest bridge they had ever seen, because everyone had built it together.

M.3.q: Why did Kit win, and how did the experience change Ploy? Answer in 3-4 sentences with evidence.
M.3.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.3.answer: Kit won because his personal story was memorable, whereas Ploy relied on numbers. Ploy, who had been furious, learned from this and now begins speeches with a person.
M.3.why: Cause: memorable story vs. numbers. Change: furious, then accepted, now starts with a person.

read.title: The Debate
sentences: Ploy was sure she would win the school debate: she had prepared for weeks and knew every statistic.
Her opponent, Kit, spoke without notes and told a short story about his grandmother instead.
When the judges announced the result, Kit had won.
Ploy was furious at first, but later she admitted that she had remembered his story and none of her numbers.
Since then, she starts every speech with a person, not a percentage.

M.3.q: Evaluate Ms. Arun's strategy. Was it better than protesting? Give an opinion and TWO reasons from the text.
M.3.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.3.answer: It was better because it solved the problem positively: forty families used the roof and the council cancelled the plan, whereas protesting had left the residents powerless.
M.3.why: Opinion with evidence: residents were powerless; the garden attracted families and changed the council's mind.

read.title: The Garden on the Roof
sentences: When the city announced plans to demolish the old market, the residents were angry but powerless.
Instead of protesting, Ms. Arun suggested turning the building's flat roof into a community garden.
Within a year, forty families were growing vegetables there, and the building, which had been scheduled for demolition, became a local landmark.
The council eventually cancelled the plans.
'We didn't fight the change,' Ms. Arun said. 'We gave the building a reason to stay.'

M.3.q: What is the theme of the story, and which sentence in the text states it most clearly? Explain your choice.
M.3.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.3.answer: The theme is that accuracy and honesty matter more than speed; the last sentence states it directly.
M.3.why: Theme: honesty/accuracy over speed. The final sentence states it. Accept a well-explained alternative.

read.title: The Translator
sentences: Hana's job was to translate for visitors at the museum, and she was proud that she never needed a dictionary.
Then a visitor used an old proverb that had no equivalent in her language.
Instead of guessing, she paused and said, 'This phrase does not translate directly; let me explain what it means.'
The visitor smiled, and the guide later said it was the most honest translation of the day.
Hana realized that being accurate sometimes matters more than being fast.

M.3.q: How do the weather and Mr. Lek's actions each contribute to the story's message? Use details.
M.3.hint: Write your answer in full sentences
M.3.answer: The storm creates the challenge and tests the tradition; Mr. Lek's example inspires others, showing that traditions continue when someone takes the first step.
M.3.why: Weather: the obstacle. Mr. Lek: leadership by example. Message: traditions survive through action and community.

read.title: The Last Day of Summer
sentences: Nobody remembered who first suggested the end-of-summer picnic, but the whole street had attended it for twenty years.
This year, a heavy storm threatened to cancel it, and several neighbors wanted to stay inside.
Mr. Lek, who was eighty, simply put on his raincoat and carried a table into the road.
One by one, the others followed, holding umbrellas and laughing at the mud.
It was the muddiest picnic anyone could remember, and, according to everyone, the best.
